_style: Address the user always with respectful plural ನೀವು / ನಿಮ್ಮ / ನಿಮಗೆ and polite imperatives (ಉಳಿಸಿ, ಕಳುಹಿಸಿ, ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸಿ); the couple together is ನೀವಿಬ್ಬರು / ನಿಮ್ಮಿಬ್ಬರ ("your story" → ನಿಮ್ಮಿಬ್ಬರ ಕಥೆ). Only ready-made words one partner sends to the other (ping texts, reactions like "Call me", letter openers) use warm intimate ನೀನು / ನಿನ್ನ ("ನಿನ್ನ ನೆನಪಾಗುತ್ತಿದೆ"). The other person is always ನಿಮ್ಮ ಸಂಗಾತಿ, never ಗಂಡ/ಹೆಂಡತಿ/ಪ್ರಿಯಕರ/ಪ್ರಿಯತಮೆ. Kannada verbs mark gender in the 3rd person (ಬಂದನು/ಬಂದಳು), so never use ಅವನು/ಅವಳು for the partner: use the neutral-respectful plural ಅವರು with -ಅರು/-ಆರೆ verb endings (ನಿಮ್ಮ ಸಂಗಾತಿ ಉತ್ತರಿಸಿದ್ದಾರೆ), or rephrase with the noun or a passive/impersonal form (ಉತ್ತರ ಬಂದಿದೆ); avoid gendered agent nouns (ಸಲಹೆಗಾರ/ಸಲಹೆಗಾರ್ತಿ). A name placeholder (%@) is never declined or given a case suffix (no %@ಗೆ, %@ರ, %@ಅವರ): rephrase so it stands alone, e.g. "%@ ಉತ್ತರಿಸಿದ್ದಾರೆ", "ಇವರಿಂದ ಪತ್ರ: %@", "%@ — ನಿಮ್ಮ ಸಂಗಾತಿ". Quotes: curly double “ ” outside, single ‘ ’ inside; ellipsis is the single character …; no space before ? ! : ; and one space after; keep the em dash — with spaces, the middle dot " · ", \n and every placeholder (%@, %lld, %1$@) exactly as in the source, reordering positional placeholders only when Kannada word order needs it. Use the Kannada script throughout with Western digits 0–9 (not ೦–೯), and let the system format dates (Kannada dates read day month year, e.g. 14 ನವೆಂಬರ್ 2026; "on a date" → "%@ ರಂದು"). Buttons are short polite verbs without ದಯವಿಟ್ಟು ("ಉಳಿಸಿ", "ಪತ್ರಕ್ಕೆ ಮುದ್ರೆ ಹಾಕಿ", "ಮತ್ತೆ ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸಿ"); tabs and chips are one or two words. Kannada has no letter case, so Latin-script brand names keep their form: Coupley, Premium, AI, CoupleSync, iCloud, iPhone. Use the ZWNJ form for English loanwords with ‘ಗಳು’ (ಸೆಟ್ಟಿಂಗ್‌ಗಳು, ವಿಜೆಟ್‌ಗಳು). Plural categories are ["one","other"]: "one" uses the singular noun (%lld ದಿನ), "other" the plural (%lld ದಿನಗಳು); with numbers prefer the natural counted form (3 ದಿನಗಳು, 5 ನೆನಪುಗಳು). Tone: warm, everyday modern Kannada as spoken in Bengaluru/Mysuru; avoid heavy Sanskritized officialese and literal word-by-word English; never cheesy.
